note: Labelled question+table→parse set for breadth step 4's table-scoped parser (Task 4). Every table is one of Task 1's eligible fixture tables under tests/fixtures/tableparse/schemas/<tableId>.json (schema+codeLists capture, metadata-only, R1). 'expect.measureCode' is a measure code copied verbatim from the table's own measure list, or 'geen' when no measure in the table answers the question. 'expect.breakdowns' has exactly one entry per offered breakdown dimension (classifyDimension === 'breakdown' — time/geo/geo_like/margins never appear here), each a member code copied verbatim from that dimension's fixture code list, 'niet_genoemd' (the question says nothing at all about that dimension — step 3's resolver then either falls to CBS's own grand total or asks, depending on whether one exists), or 'anders' (the question says something about that dimension that is not exactly one offered member: a real member the deterministic pre-filter cut, SEVERAL fitting members, or a question ACROSS the members). 'expect.periodKind' is the periodSpecSchema discriminant only. 'expect.regions' is the plain list of every place name the question names verbatim — on a table with regions, and ALSO on a table without them: when a breakdown dimension lists the place as a member, that dimension's expectation is the matching member (exactly one fits) or 'anders' (several fit, e.g. Groningen PV/ES/ET). 'expect.regionScope' (optional, absent = null) is the region class the question asks about. Two expectation forms score an expected refusal instead of a parse: measureCode 'ambiguous' with 'expect.ambiguousMeasures' (the offered measures the model cannot tell apart — same title, unit and description; the validator must throw TableParseAmbiguousMeasureError), and 'expect.outcome': 'region_unavailable' (a named place the table cannot serve; the validator must throw TableParseRegionUnavailableError). Every case's expectation is also run through the real validator by the integrity test, so a label that contradicts the validator's own rules fails CI. Every code was checked against the real fixture (measure lists, dimension code lists) and, for truncated dimensions (>MEMBER_PROMPT_CAP members), against buildTableParseSchema's ACTUAL offered list for that exact question text — not guessed. Grand-total resolvability per dimension (used to write honest 'falls to total' vs 'no total' cases) was checked with src/query/breakdowns.ts's own findGrandTotal, not assumed from the title alone. Category minimums (brief): geen ≥4, niet_genoemd-falls-to-total ≥4 (id prefix 'total-'; several more appear incidentally in other cases), anders ≥3, two-totals/no-total dimension ≥3 (id prefix 'nototal-'; a couple more appear incidentally), region ≥2 (a couple more appear incidentally via explicit 'Nederland' mentions), period-grain-unavailable ≥2 (id prefix 'grain-') — every one of these minimums, and the exact per-category counts, is enforced by tests/answer/table-parse/labelled-set.test.ts, not restated here as a number that could drift out of sync with the case list below. The remaining cases (id prefix 'general-') are happy-path breadth across the remaining tables/dimensions/period kinds. Controller-ruling correction: the brief guessed 'probably 03759ned' as the one fixture table with regions — buildTableParseSchema (run against every eligible fixture) shows BOTH 03759ned and 84521NED have hasRegions=true (both have a GeoDimension-kind RegioS). The 2 designated region cases use 03759ned; 84521NED's regions are not exercised in this set (left for a later step). Final-review fix wave (2026-09-29): region names on region-coded breakdown dimensions (85004NED RegioS, 82291NED CaribischNederland), the widened 'anders', the ambiguous-measure form and one region-unavailable case were added; see the individual case notes. Breadth step 5, Task 7 (2026-09-29): follow-up cases (id prefix 'followup-') carry an optional 'previousQuestion' — the previous table-lane question in the same conversation, which the parser reads as its 'Vorige vraag in dit gesprek' line (prompt version 3) and the member pre-filter reads too, exactly as planTableLane builds them (scripts/tableparse-eval.ts caseParseInput). Their expectations follow the follow-up rule: whatever the new question does not name (topic, period, place, breakdown) is carried over from the previous question; a new question that names another topic the table lacks is 'geen'.
